what_happened: The design job "Design overlapping CI waits with producer work" was rejected at the final verdict. 2 of 6 acceptance criteria were unmet. (1) The Existing code section did not properly reuse or extend the three named design docs or say which of their rules change. (2) The note did not state how the next throughput review would measure the saving. The verifier also raised three major findings and no blockers. Change (3), pushing the candidate when the producer ends, already exists in the code, but the note presents it as new and misstates the current rule. The scoring method uses the `checks` stage, which leaves out both CI waits, so it cannot measure the saving. The Existing code table credits a made-up rule to agent-and-build-slots.md and does not cite the code that actually waits for base CI. No failed checks are listed.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that checks a note's claims about what is new, its attributed rules and its measurement method against the existing code and the recorded stage data. The note was written from the request's framing and the neighbouring design docs, not from the landing code. It therefore proposed a change that already exists, credited a rule to the wrong doc, and chose a stage to score that excludes the waits it targets. Criteria check that sections exist, not that each claim matches the code or that the scoring stage covers the saving. Only the verifier reads the code and records, at the end. This is the fifth landing-design job to fail this way.
prevention: Add a required survey step to every design job before the note is drafted. The producer writes an Existing code inventory: for each proposed change, the file and function that does it today, or a statement that none exists. For each rule attributed to a doc, it gives the quoted line. For the scoring method, it names the recorded stage that spans the saving and checks it against a real job's records. Acceptance criteria for design jobs should require the inventory entries and the citations, and a code check should confirm that every cited path and line exists. The reading should also list the changelog and the cited docs as deliverables to reconcile.
proposed_request: Redo the design note docs/design/overlap-ci-waits.md on overlapping CI waits with producer work, fixing the three major findings from job 20261110-191311-r241. Before drafting, survey the code and write the Existing code section from it. For each of the three changes, name the file and function that does it today, or say none does. Change (3), pushing the candidate when the producer ends, already exists, so say what it does now and what, if anything, would still change. Quote the real rule from docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md (lines 173-174), agent-and-build-slots.md and continuous-landing.md, and state which of their rules change. Cite the code that waits for base CI. Rewrite the measurement section so the next throughput review compares a named stage that includes both CI waits, using median minutes per landed job against the prediction. Check the method against the stage records of at least one real recent job and show that the stage spans the waits. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Only docs and CHANGELOG.md may change.
